name: Seated Cable Row High Pull
description: The seated cable row high pull uses a rope attachment at a low or mid cable position and pulls toward the face/neck rather than the abdomen, with elbows flaring wide at shoulder height. It bridges the gap between a standard row and a face pull, training the rear deltoids, upper trapezius, and external rotators through a horizontally-abducted pulling pattern while seated.

execution.starting_position: Sit facing a cable pulley set at low or mid-height. Attach a rope. Grip with both hands, arms extended forward.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust cable height so the pull angle targets the face/upper chest. Sit far enough from the stack to allow full arm extension.
steps: Step 1: Begin seated with arms extended gripping the rope.
Step 2: Pull the rope toward the face/forehead, driving elbows wide and high.
Step 3: At peak, elbows should be at or above shoulder height, hands beside the ears.
Step 5: Return under control to full arm extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Pulling to the chest instead of the face — the high pull targets rear delts, not lats
Elbows dropping below shoulder height — keep them elevated
safety_considerations: Light loads recommended — rear delts and external rotators are small muscles
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to hands beside face with elbows at shoulder height.
coaching_cues: Pull to the face, not the belly
Thumbs point back at the peak
